prompt:

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Outfit: a perfumer look fitted to her body — a silk blouse slipped off both shoulders, a corset belt, a short skirt and stockings, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body turned three-quarters toward the camera; head tilted slightly; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a small perfume bottle up beside her face; it is all she holds.
EXPRESSION: crinkled lower eyelids, closed-lip smile pushing the cheeks up, brows relaxed.
Scene note: she is a perfumer testing a new blend

Framing: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — bromine: the only nonmetal that is liquid at room temperature, a heavy red-brown liquid that breathes off orange-red fumes; named from the Greek for 'stench' after Antoine-Jérôme Balard drew it from the bitter brine left in the salt marshes of Montpellier in 1826; the bromine inside the molecule of Tyrian purple, the royal dye wrung from murex sea snails; silver bromide in the gelatin dry plates that caught the light of photographs; flame retardants that smother fire; lavish, decadent, dangerous to breathe — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
